title: Tiger Woods
wiki_lead:
Eldrick Tont "Tiger" Woods (born December 30, 1975) is an American professional golfer. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest golfers of all time and as one of the most famous athletes in modern history. Woods is tied for first in PGA Tour wins, ranks second in men's major championships, holds numerous golf records, and is an inductee of the World Golf Hall of Fame.
Following an outstanding junior, college, and amateur career, Woods turned professional in 1996 at age 20. In April 1997 he won his first major, the 1997 Masters, which he won by 12 strokes in a record-setting performance. He reached number one in the Official World Golf Ranking for the first time in June 1997, less than a year after turning professional. At the 2000 U.S. Open Woods won by a major record 15 strokes which is regarded by many as the greatest performance in golf history. After winning the 2001 Masters he became the only player to win four consecutive major championships in a one-year period in a feat known as the "Tiger Slam". Woods dominated men's golf throughout the first decade of the 21st century, holding the world's top ranking from August 1999 to September 2004 (264 consecutive weeks) and again from June 2005 to October 2010 (281 consecutive weeks). The following decade was marked by comebacks from personal issues and injuries. He took a self‑imposed hiatus from professional golf from December 2009 to April 2010 to address marital problems. Woods fell to number 58 in the world rankings in November 2011 before returning to the number‑one position between March 2013 and May 2014. Injuries led to four back surgeries between 2014 and 2017, and he competed in only one tournament between August 2015 and January 2018, dropping out of the world's top 1,000 players. After returning to regular competition, he won the Tour Championship in September 2018—his first victory in five years—and the 2019 Masters, his first major in 11 years.
Woods holds numerous golf records. He has spent the most consecutive weeks and the most total weeks as the world's number‑one player. He has been named PGA Player of the Year a record 11 times, and he led the PGA Tour money list in 10 seasons. He has won 15 major golf championships (second only to Jack Nicklaus's 18) and 82 PGA Tour events (tied with Sam Snead for the all-time record). Woods is one of six men to complete the career Grand Slam, along with Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Nicklaus, and Rory McIlroy. He is the youngest to do so, and one of two golfers—along with Nicklaus—to achieve the career Grand Slam three times. He was a member of the winning United States team at the 1999 Ryder Cup and received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in May 2019.
Woods was awarded AP Athlete of the Year four times and AP Athlete of the Decade of the 2000s. He was also awarded Sports Illustrated Sportsperson of the Year three times and the Laureus World Sports Sportsman of the Year twice. Woods was among Time's 100 most influential people in the world in 2004, 2009 and 2019, which is tied for the second most selections for a professional athlete. He has been listed by Forbes as the highest paid athlete in the world for a record 11 years, including for 10 straight years from 2002 to 2011. As of April 2026, his net worth was estimated at US$1.5 billion by Forbes.
On February 23, 2021, Woods was hospitalized after a single‑car collision and underwent emergency surgery for compound fractures in his right leg and a shattered ankle. In a November 2021 interview with Golf Digest, he stated that his full‑time professional career was over, though he intended to play a limited schedule. He returned to the PGA Tour at the 2022 Masters. In 2026, Woods was involved in another car crash and reached a plea deal for willful reckless driving.

grok_lead: Tiger Woods, born Eldrick Tont Woods on December 30, 1975, in Cypress, California, is an American professional golfer widely regarded as one of the greatest in the sport's history. He turned professional in 1996 at age 20 and has amassed 82 victories on the PGA Tour, tying the all-time record held by Sam Snead. Woods has won 15 major championships, including five Masters Tournaments, four PGA Championships, three U.S. Opens, and three Open Championships, second only to Jack Nicklaus's 18 majors. His career earnings on the PGA Tour exceed $120 million, and he has been named PGA Player of the Year a record 11 times. Woods's dominance includes holding the world number one ranking for a cumulative 683 weeks, the most in history, and achieving the "Tiger Slam" by winning four consecutive majors from 2000 to 2001. The son of Earl Woods, a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel, and Kultida Woods, a native of Thailand, he earned his nickname " Tiger " in honor of a Vietnamese soldier and close friend of his father. Woods displayed prodigious talent from infancy, putting on a backyard course at six months old and appearing on The Mike Douglas Show at age two, where he defeated Bob Hope in a putting contest. By age three, he shot 48 over nine holes, and at five, he was profiled in Golf Digest as the "Wunderkind of Golf." As an amateur, he won three U.S. Junior Amateur Championships (1991â1993) and three consecutive U.S. Amateur titles (1994â1996), the youngest winner in each event's history. At Stanford University, he captured the NCAA individual championship in 1996 before leaving after two years to join the professional tour. Woods's professional breakthrough came swiftly; in 1997, at 21 years and three months, he became the youngest Masters champion and won by a record 12-stroke margin, ushering in an era of global popularity for golf often called the "Tiger Effect." He completed the career Grand Slam by age 24 and held all four major titles simultaneously in 2001, the only player to do so. Beyond competition, Woods is an entrepreneur and philanthropist; he founded the TGR Foundation in 1996, which supports education through the TGR Learning Lab, and TGR Design, his golf course architecture firm that has created courses like Bluejack National. Woods's career has been marked by personal and physical challenges, including a 2009 public scandal involving infidelity that led to a divorce in 2010 and a temporary hiatus from golf. He underwent multiple back surgeries starting in 2014, culminating in his seventh procedureâa lumbar disc replacementâin October 2025 to address a collapsed disc and chronic pain. A severe car accident in February 2021 resulted in leg fractures and additional surgeries, limiting his play, while a torn Achilles tendon sidelined him for much of 2025. Despite these setbacks, Woods staged a remarkable comeback to win his 15th major at the 2019 Masters, his last PGA Tour victory to date. In March 2026, he returned to competitive action in the TGL Finals after more than a year away. On March 27, 2026, Woods registered for the 2026 U.S. Senior Open at Scioto Country Club, his first entry into a senior major after turning 50 in December 2025, though he has not committed to playing and will decide later. President Donald Trump stated on March 26 that Woods would attend the 2026 Masters but not compete, despite Woods indicating he wants to play if his body allows. On March 27, 2026, he was arrested in Jupiter Island, Florida (Martin County), on suspicion of DUI following a rollover crash involving his Land Rover Range Rover SUV just after 2 p.m. ET. He attempted to pass a truck, clipped its trailer, and the vehicle rolled over. Woods exited the vehicle unaided and was held for processing; neither Woods nor the other driver was injured. Authorities observed signs of impairment, possibly from medication (breathalyzer registered 0.00 with no alcohol detected), but he refused a urine test, leading to misdemeanor charges of DUI with property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test. No immediate statement was issued by Woods or his representatives; he was arrested at the scene. He continues to influence the sport through course design, team ownership in TGL, and advisory roles on the PGA Tour's future direction, even as his playing schedule remains limited due to health issues.
